title: UK Graduate Visa From Jan 2027: 18 or 24 Months?
excerpt: From 1 January 2027 most UK Graduate visas are 18 months, PhD graduates keep three years and graduates of some universities keep two. See the key date and what to do.

content.html:
🎓 UK Graduate Visa From 2027 — At a Glance
Key Date1 January 2027 (Application Date)
Bachelor's / Master's18 Months if You Apply From 1 Jan 2027
Apply Before 1 Jan 2027Current 2 Years Still Applies
PhD Graduates3 Years (No Change)
Selected Universities2 Years Planned; List Not Published
ExtensionNot Possible — Switch Visa Instead

What Is Changing

The UK Graduate visa is moving to a tiered system. The rule that matters most is the date you apply, not the date you started your course.

GroupGraduate visa length
Bachelor's or master's graduate, applying before 1 January 20272 years (current rule)
Bachelor's or master's graduate, applying on or after 1 January 202718 months
Graduate of a "high compliance" university with strong labor market outcomes2 years, as announced in the 2026 Budget (details not published)
PhD graduate3 years, no change
⚠️
Two things are still unclearThe government has not published which universities count as "high compliance" or the test they must pass, and it has not given a date for doing so. Do not rely on any list you see online.

Why the Application Date Matters

University immigration teams describe the 18-month rule as applying to successful applications made on or after 1 January 2027. If you apply under the Graduate route before that date, you keep the current two-year duration.

You can only apply after you have completed your course and your university has reported this to the Home Office. So the question is whether your course ends, and your university completes its reporting, in time for you to apply before 1 January 2027.

ℹ️
Check with your universityAsk your international office for your official course completion date and when it will report it. Confirm the timing in writing.

What It Means If You Are Studying Now

  • Course ending in 2026: you may be able to apply before 1 January 2027. Check your end date and your visa expiry date with your university.
  • Course ending in 2027 or later: plan for 18 months unless your university is later named as a two-year institution.
  • PhD students: the three-year Graduate visa stays the same.

What It Means If You Are Applying for 2027

If you are choosing a UK university for a 2027 intake, plan around 18 months after graduation as the safe baseline. A university that qualifies for two years would be a bonus, not something to count on yet.

  • Compare universities: ask each one whether it expects to qualify as high compliance and what its graduate outcomes look like.
  • Check the compliance record: look at its visa refusal and enrolment history, and whether it is on a Home Office action plan.
  • Budget for 18 months: plan how you will find a skilled job, or switch to another visa such as Skilled Worker, within that time.
  • Keep your course fit: a strong course and clear career plan matter more than any one visa rule.

The Graduate Visa Cannot Be Extended

The Graduate visa is a temporary route. It cannot be extended, and it does not lead directly to settlement. To stay longer you would need to switch to another route, such as a Skilled Worker visa, before it expires.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does the 18-month Graduate visa start?
For bachelor's and master's graduates, it applies to successful applications made on or after 1 January 2027.
Can I still get two years?
Yes if you apply before 1 January 2027, or if your university is later named a high-compliance university that keeps the two-year duration.
Do PhD graduates lose a year?
No. PhD graduates keep a three-year Graduate visa.
Which universities will keep two years?
No list or criteria have been published yet.
Can I extend my Graduate visa?
No. You would need to switch to another visa, such as Skilled Worker, before it ends.
Does my course start date matter?
The reported rule depends on when you apply, not when you began your course. Confirm the details for your case with your university.
